notes:
Snapshot: mid-market product analytics startup (B2B SaaS) evaluating Redwood Hosted API during Q1 trial; now progressed to Dedicated sizing conversation.

Trial observations (hosted API):
- Trial period: 2026-01-10 -> 2026-02-28 (self-serve + AE demos).
- Active seats during trial: ~420 MAUs; 850 unique sessions; 1,250 requests/day average; peak 3,500 req/day during product launch window.
- Observed QPS: avg 0.015 QPS sustained; peak 0.9 QPS observed in 90th percentile windows.
- Concurrency seen during peak test: 18 concurrent active generation streams.
- Token mix (trial): 72% short (<150 tokens), 24% medium (150-800 tokens), 4% long (>800 tokens). Average tokens/request: ~240 tokens.
- Latency: hosted avg 160ms; p95 ~480ms for chat generation.
- Failure modes: occasional 429s at extreme peaks; acceptable fallbacks in trial but want SLA for production.

Product & requirements summary:
- Primary workloads: conversational product assistant (chat), document search/semantic rank (embeddings + reranking), nightly batch summarization jobs.
- Targets: p95 latency <=250ms for chat; throughput target of sustained 50 QPS during peak growth windows; concurrency target ~120 concurrent requests for planned 6x growth.
- Cost sensitivity: mid-market ARR profile; prefer reserved capacity commit to lower unit cost vs hosted pay-as-you-go. Need clear unit economics per token and per-hour GPU commit.
- Model preferences: open-ish family (Llama-family and other open models), willing to test quantized variants; require model version pinning + canary rollout.
- Routing/fallback: want automatic fallback to smaller (cheaper) model when Dedicated pool under pressure; also geographic routing EU/NA.

Dedicated sizing recommendation (initial proposal):
- Baseline reserve: 4x GPU slots (A10/A100-equivalent) with autoscale burst to +2 standby GPUs for spikes. This aligns to projected sustained 50 QPS with p95 latency target.
- Concurrency planning: plan for 120 concurrent token streams (concurrency headroom 2.5x measured trial peak).
- Token budget forecast (monthly): current trial ~12M tokens/month. 6-month forecast (3x growth) -> ~36M tokens/month; 12-month forecast -> ~90M tokens/month.
- Suggested config: enable KV/prefix caching for repeated prompts, continuous batching window 40ms, 16-bit quantized model for cost savings in non-critical routes.
- Fallback plan: route non-critical summarization to lower-cost model pool; keep chat on higher-quality pinned model.

POC & procurement timeline (CRM timeline):
- 2026-01-12: Intro demo with AE (Morgan) + SE (Jordan) — basic hosted API walkthrough. (gt-2026-01-12-hrx939)
- 2026-01-15: Trial onboarding + Fireflies transcript ff-20260115-9842; team ran initial load tests.
- 2026-02-21: Deep-dive on security & residency — Fireflies ff-20260221-1123; asked for SOC2 + KMS details.
- 2026-03-03: SE sizing workshop; Jordan shared reference config and cost calc.
- 2026-03-09: Pricing review call with finance; requested Dedicated committed pricing + SOW.

Decision criteria (what matters to buyer):
- Predictable unit cost and clear amortized GPU pricing (primary).
- Security controls: SSO/SAML, KMS, audit logs, SOC2.
- Regional residency for EU customers.
- Performance: p95 latency & predictable concurrency under load.

Open items / blockers:
- Legal needs explicit data residency SLA for EU-hosted Dedicated pools.
- Finance needs 3-year ARR model showing payback on Dedicated commit vs hosted.
- KMS integration: timeline to support customer KMS (HSM) for keys.

Next steps (short):
- Deliver formal Dedicated sizing + pricing proposal with two tiers (conservative and aggressive) by 2026-03-17 (action: AE).
- Technical call between Redwood infra security and SageHarbor infra to confirm KMS/data residency feasibility (action: SE).
- Legal to receive SOW draft and redline by end of March.
